newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-WOODS STRUGGLES TO MAKE IMPACT AT MASTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS STRUGGLES TO MAKE IMPACT AT MASTERS.

text.p: Australian Peter OMalley fired a level par 73 to take a one shot lead after the third round of the Australian Masters on Saturday as American Tiger Woods struggled to make an impact.
OMalley, who raced to 15 under par after 36 holes at the tight Huntingdale layout, holds the narrow lead over compatriot and joint overnight leader Lucas Parsons.
After two days of low scoring, Parsons and OMalley enjoyed a four-shot lead at the start of the day but their troubles allowed the chasing pack to narrow the gap.
Australian pair Robert Allenby and Wayne Grady took most advantage by moving to 13 under, two shots adrift of OMalley and one behind Parsons, who shot 74 on Saturday.
Woods, however, could manage no better than a one-under par 72 in his third round to end the day six shots behind the leader.
Woods, who won the Bangkok Classic on Sunday, said he was unable to read the fast greens at Hungtingdale.
"Im hitting good putts but they seem to want not to go in. Im all around the edges," Woods said.
He said his swing had developed a couple of minor faults.
OMalley said he would need to finish on at least 20 under par for the tournament to win on Sunday.
"Ill have to go out there and hit five or six under," OMalley said.
